round1_to_round2.note: All five took the round-1 corrections: core EPS without the $2.98 of H1 gains, NTM = 1/3 FY28 + 2/3 FY29, about 787M post-ASR shares, SBC at 9% of revenue, and no ASR double count in FY29. The fair-value spread narrowed from $30 to $15 and the mean fell about $6. Every agent trimmed its upper tail; agent_3 raised its left side. The 1-month ladders did not change.

revision_check.residual_issues: FY29 core EPS of $18.4 (net income +11%, shares -1.5%, about +13% EPS) is still the most aggressive of the five, given organic growth that has held at 7-8% for five quarters. The 6.25% FCF yield is justified by the ~5.9% the market pays today, which partly anchors fair value to the price. Its $256 is the high end, and about $4 of that comes from these two choices.

SBC, gains, shares and deal-cash net debt are all corrected. Two issues remain. The bear story uses about $33B of net debt while the fair-value method uses $29B. And its ladder still implies a mean of about $260, above its own $251 fair value; P(>=405) of 0.085 is the fattest of the five.

It keeps 14x and a 6.5% yield, with a stated reason (7-8% organic growth, leverage, an unrerated multiple). That is a defensible disagreement, not an error. The Moody's rating is corrected to A2 stable, and the S&P outlook is flagged as unverified. No residual errors.

The NTM EPS and FY29 double count are fixed, and vendor blogs are now treated as anecdote. However, its ladder has the highest P(>=231) of the five (0.572) despite the second-lowest fair value ($244), and its tails are the thinnest (P>=162 of 0.871, P>=405 of 0.035). The distribution is tighter than the 47% vol it cites, and its median sits above spot for no stated reason.
revision_check.verdict: acceptable, ladder shape inconsistent with its own fair value

disagreements.topic: Is the $241-256 fair value vs $231 spot real edge?
disagreements.positions: All five now sit 4-11% above spot (mean $248.4). The ladder mean implies an expected price of about $252.
disagreements.resolution: Mostly not. Today's NTM core EPS is about $15.7 (roughly Q4 FY27 about $3.6 on the post-ASR count plus 3/4 of FY28 about $16.2), so $231 is about 14.7x. The agents apply 14-14.5x to a Sep-2027 NTM EPS of about $17.5. So nearly the whole gap is one year of EPS accretion at an unchanged-to-slightly-lower multiple. About half of that accretion is the debt-funded ASR, which is leverage rather than organic growth. A +7-9% one-year price drift is roughly the cost of equity for a levered, ~45%-vol software name, and it matches agent_5's mature-software base rate (ORCL/ADBE median +8%). This is carry, not mispricing. Real edge would require a re-rating, and the evidence for one (organic reacceleration) is not yet in hand.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' own EPS builds; Q2 FY27 8-K Ex.99.1 (Q3 guide $3.42-3.44 on 827M); agent_5 Twelve Data base-rate computation.

disagreements.topic: Organic growth durability (drives the bull weight)
disagreements.positions: All five hold a 25% bull weight at $315-340, which assumes a re-rating to 17.5-19x on organic reacceleration to 10%+.
disagreements.resolution: Organic growth has been flat at about 7-8% for five straight quarters. Q4 FY26 organic revenue was about 8% and organic cRPO about 9% CC once Informatica's ~4pts are stripped. Q1 FY27 core apps grew 7% CC with attrition steady at about 8%. The Q3 FY27 guide implies about 7-8% again. The H2 reacceleration is a promise backed by strong NNAOV, not an observed trend, and headline reacceleration has so far been acquisition-driven. I trim the upper tail modestly; I do not cut the bull weight outright, because the December print could still deliver.
disagreements.evidence: SaaStr analysis of Q1 FY27 (core Agentforce Apps +7% CC, cRPO 13% CC, attrition ~8%); Q4 FY26 organic ~8% / organic cRPO ~9% CC (search summary of company-reported figures); Q2 FY27 release Q3 guide.

disagreements.topic: Leadership change: one departure or a pattern
disagreements.positions: All five now cite only the Tallapragada transition (effective 2026-08-06) as execution risk.
disagreements.resolution: The churn is broader, and all of it is public and months old. Five senior exits by Feb 2026: Slack CEO (to OpenAI), Tableau CEO, CMO, CSO, and Agentforce head Adam Evans. Six replacements followed, including Madhav Thattai as Agentforce GM and Joe Inzerillo as President of Enterprise and AI Technology. In Aug 2026 Miguel Milano was promoted to COO, and Rohan Kumar (joined June) took over engineering. The CEO is unchanged. This supports keeping the ~23-25% bear weight rather than raising it. It is priced news, but it lowers the odds of flawless Agentforce execution needed for the bull re-rating.
disagreements.evidence: People Matters 2026-02-11 (five exits, six appointments); SalesforceBen on the Milano COO promotion (Aug 2026); 8-K 2026-08-05.

disagreements.positions: Bear weights 23-25% at $155-165 across all agents; no agent has hard seat data.
disagreements.resolution: Still unresolved. Salesforce no longer discloses seats. Management says customers buy agents on top of seats, and attrition is steady at about 8%. The Agentforce ARR definition was widened in Q2 FY27. No independent seat data has surfaced. I keep the bear weight at the mean; the Q3 print (early December, date not yet announced) is the test.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 FY27 release; SaaStr Q1 FY27 analysis; Q2 call summaries.

one_month_reasoning: No earnings fall in the window (the Q3 FY27 date is not yet announced; early December is typical). The in-window events are the ASR final settlement (~34M shares, known), the Fin close, ServiceNow and Microsoft prints in late October, and the FOMC. So I keep the agents' near-symmetric mean centred on spot with ~12.5-13% monthly sigma. The five agents agree to within 0.02 at every strike.
confidence_reason: Round 2 has no remaining computational disagreement; the agents converged on the round-1 corrections. My searches found persistent 7-8% organic growth and broader leadership churn. Both support a slightly thinner right tail, but neither settles the seat-erosion question, which only the December print can. The tilt is small, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: About 10x a ~$16.2 FY28 core EPS, near the June-2026 trough ($146-178). Below it the market is pricing an actual seat-base decline or a failed organic reacceleration (organic cRPO under ~8%, an FY28 guide under ~8%), not 45%-vol noise. The $182-average ASR would also be deeply underwater on ~$39B of debt.
key_drivers: Organic growth has been stuck at 7-8% for five quarters (organic cRPO ~9% CC). The H2 reacceleration promised on NNAOV strength is untested until the early-December Q3 print, and it is the only path to a re-rating.

The gap to fair value is carry, not mispricing: ~14.7x current NTM core EPS (~$15.7) vs ~14-14.5x on Sep-2027 NTM (~$17.5). About half the EPS growth is the debt-funded ASR (~787M shares after October settlement).
Leverage: ~$39B of debt, ~$29B net debt after ~$5.1B for Contentful and Fin, and Moody's A2 stable. Interest is already in the run-rate.
Leadership churn through 2026 (Agentforce head, Slack and Tableau CEOs, CMO, CSO, then the engineering president; new COO in Aug) during the Agentforce execution test.
AI seat erosion is unmeasured: seats are undisclosed, attrition is steady at ~8%, and the Agentforce ARR definition was widened.

fair_value.reason: 50/50 of (a) ~14.25x Sep-2027 NTM core EPS of ~$17.5 (1/3 FY28 ~$16.2 + 2/3 FY29 ~$18.1, ~787M post-ASR shares, no investment gains) = ~$249, and (b) SBC-adjusted NTM FCF of ~$12.3B / ~787M = ~$15.7 at 6.4% = ~$245. I lowered the multiple from 14.5x in round 1 because organic growth shows no reacceleration yet and leadership churn is broader than one departure. The agent mean is $248.4; this is +7% vs spot, roughly a cost-of-equity return.

summary: All five forecasters took the round-1 corrections, and the fair values converged to $241-256 (mean $248). The gap to the $231 spot is mostly not edge. It is one year of EPS accretion at an unchanged ~14-14.5x multiple, about half of it from the debt-funded ASR, which is roughly the cost of equity for a levered 45%-vol name and matches the mature-software base rate of about +8%. Organic growth has sat at 7-8% for five quarters, and 2026 leadership churn is broader than the one departure the agents cite, so I trim the upper tail slightly and keep the mean otherwise. The early-December Q3 print is the real catalyst, and conviction is low until it shows organic reacceleration.
